question: I work full time during the day. Are there any majors at Ramapo that can be completed entirely online or through evening classes?
answer:
Yes—there are flexible options, but the pages do not say that every major can be completed entirely online. Ramapo offers online classes in all disciplines; consult your advisor about details [7].

For returning adult students, the Degree Completion Program offers 8-week in-person evening courses meeting once a week on the Mahwah campus, or 15-week fully online courses that do not require campus attendance. Both pathways lead to a BA [8, 10]. The program is described as accommodating full-time working professionals [8]. Hybrid classes meet once a week from 6:05-9:35 p.m. Monday or Thursday; fully online classes are asynchronous with no scheduled class meetings [14]. These are course formats, not a statement that every major can be completed entirely online.

The pages differ in how they name the accelerated majors: Social Science and Contemporary Arts: Professional Communication [8, 11, 15]; Social Science and Interdisciplinary Studies [10, 13]; and Social Science/Justice [15]. Check with the program about which major and format fits your situation.

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7300 [8, 10]. Degree Completion Program: contact Patricia Laprey, Director of Degree Completion, at plaprey@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7388 [15].

Sources: [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/returning-student/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/adult-degree-completion/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/degree-completion-program/)

question: Does Ramapo offer a degree completion program for adults who already have an associate's degree? If so, what are the requirements?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers the Degree Completion Program (DCP), with accelerated majors in Social Science: Society and Culture concentration and Interdisciplinary Studies. [9] It is designed for people with an associate’s degree or at least 64 credits from prior institutions. [5][9] The pages differ on age: one says designed for adults 25 or older [5]; another says DCP students are typically 24 or older. [9]

For program enrollment, 48 transfer credits are the minimum and 60 are recommended. [7] DCP students apply using the Transfer Student application. [9] To apply, visit https://apply.ramapo.edu/apply/; the program page also links to information for applicants at https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/. [8]

The Degree Completion Program page lists the director, Patricia Laprey, as a contact for questions about whether the program is right for you: plaprey@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7388. [7]

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/faqs/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/adult-students/adult-degree-completion/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/dcp/) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/dcp/program-overview-and-eligibility/)

question: If I already completed English Composition at my county college, does that satisfy the writing requirement in Ramapo's gen ed?
answer:
A completed English Composition course by itself is not confirmed here as satisfying Ramapo’s Critical Reading and Writing II requirement. All students must complete the reading and writing requirements by 64 earned credits [8]; Critical Reading and Writing II is a required general education course [11].

For an individual course, contact the Vice Provost to review it and its potential for transfer credit. If the Vice Provost approves the equivalency, approval goes to Admissions to update the appropriate systems [10]. Contact the Office of the Provost: provost@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7330. Course evaluation policy: https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1 [10].

If you completed an A.A. or A.S. degree at a New Jersey community college, the published pages say you can fulfill/be waived from general education requirements; the waiver is once Ramapo receives a final official transcript showing the conferred degree. An A.A.S. does not qualify for a full waiver; courses are evaluated individually [12][14].

Sources: [8](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education-reading-writing-and-mathematics) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#transferring-academic-credit1) [11](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#general-education) [12](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/agreements/) [14](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/)

question: What does CMPS 147 cover, and is there a prerequisite I need before enrolling in it?
answer:
CMPS 147 COMPUTER SCIENCE I is 4 credits. It introduces problem-solving with computers, including basic computer-system concepts; ANSI C++ programming; algorithm design; program development, debugging, testing and documentation; and variables, data types, expressions, selection, repetition, functions and arrays. A course fee is required. It carries the Gen Ed 18-Quantitative Rsng (GEQR) attribute. [1]

Before registering, satisfactorily complete one of these courses: MATH 021 PREPARATION FOR COLLEGE MATHEMATICS PROGRAM; MATH 022 TRANSITIONAL MATHEMATICS; MATH 024 ELEMENTARY ALGEBRA TOPICS; MATH 100T TRANSFER GE MATH EQUIVALENT; MATH 101 MATH WITH APPLICATIONS; MATH 104 MATH FOR THE MODERN WORLD; MATH 108 ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; MATH 110 PRECALCULUS; or MATH 121 CALCULUS I. Alternatively, complete one placement test with the minimum score: ACCUPLACER Quantitative Reasoning 258; ACCUPLACER Advanced Algebra and Functions 260; ACT Composite 26; or SAT MATH 580. [1]

The Registrar says to review prerequisite requirements in Web Self Service and course descriptions there. Transfer or visiting students who fulfilled the prerequisite but cannot register should contact the academic school offering the course. If you prove you satisfied it, the unit secretary may place an override on your record; then complete registration in Experience: https://experience.elluciancloud.com/rconj/. [3] Contact the Registrar at reg@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7695. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/courses/CMPS147) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/registrationinfo/)

question: I am interested in nursing but I can only attend part time. What is the recommended sequence of courses for someone starting the nursing program?
answer:
The Nursing Generic BSN is the track for students interested in becoming nurses; its recommended plan is for students admitted in 2026–2027. It is not identified as a part-time plan. The Accelerated BSN is explicitly a full-time, daytime, in-person program [1,2].

Recommended Nursing Generic BSN sequence [2]:
• First year, Fall (17 credits): INTD 101, CHEM 111/111L, CRWT 102, General Education, PATH 001.
• First year, Spring (16): General Education ×2, PSYC 101, MATH 108.
• Second year, Fall: General Education ×2, BIOL 214/214L, free elective, PATH 002.
• Second year, Spring (15): General Education, BIOL 216/216L, BIOL 212/212L, PATH 003.
• Third year, Fall (16): NURS 305, 306, 325, 330.
• Third year, Spring (16): NURS 340, 345, 355, 370.
• Fourth year, Fall (16): NURS 410, 425, 430, 435.
• Fourth year, Spring (16): NURS 440, 475, 450, 470.
Total required: 128 credits. The plan lists another track for that year, Nursing/RN/BSN [2]. Nursing Generic BSN also publishes Nursing MSN [2].

The plan does not say how to follow this sequence part time. Contact the Nursing Programs Office: (201) 684-7749, Adler Center for Nursing Excellence 215.

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG)

question: Does Ramapo have any certificate programs that a working adult could finish without completing a full bachelor's degree?
answer:
Ramapo’s catalog lists seven certificates: Applied Ethics; Business Essentials; Business Foundations-Graduate; Data Analyst-Graduate; Data Modeler-Graduate; Machine Learning Engineer-Graduate; and Spanish for Health Care and Human Services Professionals. [3] Graduate certificates require at least 9 credits beyond the bachelor’s level. [4] Business Essentials is specifically identified as a Graduate Certificate, so it does not appear to be an option to finish without a bachelor’s degree. [1][4] The catalog does not specify the level for Applied Ethics or Spanish for Health Care and Human Services Professionals, so I can’t verify whether those can be completed without a bachelor’s degree. [3][4]

Ramapo welcomes non-degree/visiting students who are interested in an academic certificate, but that page lists Business Essentials, Graduate Certificate in Business Foundations, Middle School Teacher, Spanish for Healthcare and Human Services Professionals, and Investigative Genetic Genealogy; its list differs from the catalog’s. It does not say that taking non-degree courses lets you complete a certificate without a bachelor’s degree. [9][3]

For clarification, contact Admissions at admissions@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7300, or the Office of the Provost at provost@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7330. [9][4]

question: Which gen ed categories can be satisfied by a single course, and is there a limit on how many gen ed courses can also count toward my major?
answer:
A single course may not fulfill two separate General Education competencies [2]. You take one course in each keystone category—Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning—and one course in two of the three distribution categories [7]. For Fall 2026, the distribution categories are Culture and Creativity, Values and Ethics, and Social Systems and Society [5]. The College’s catalog also lists the keystone and distribution requirements [8].

No more than two General Education courses may count both toward General Education and your major [2].
